subject: Medigenics — hosting route & audit playbook
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@medigenics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Medigenics — hosting route & audit playbook

Hi Laura — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we keep momentum with your internal stakeholders (security + procurement):

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary requirement: PHI handling for the new clinical triage feature (HIPAA scope).
- Must have a signed BAA in place before production.
- Medigenics security wants SOC 2 Type II evidence and encryption-at-rest keys ownership details.
- Preference: minimal operational burden on your infra team; but CX and uptime targets may push toward Dedicated capacity if you need sustained throughput.

Redwood hosting route options (short):
1) Hosted API — fastest to prod, Redwood-managed keys, shared tenancy. Requires BAA & SOC 2 in-scope controls. Good if traffic is spiky and you want minimal ops.
2) Dedicated capacity — reserved GPU pools in our environment, isolated tenancy. Provides stronger isolation and predictable performance; still Redwood-managed infra but we can scope additional audit controls.
3) Private (VPC / on-prem) — customer-controlled network and key ownership. Required if your audit team insists on customer KMS or fully air-gapped flows. Longer lead time (infra & network setup).

Asks / next steps: 
- Laura: can you share the exact SOC 2 evidence packet your auditors need (control IDs or a checklist)? We attached our SOC2-Report-2024.pdf stub for reference.
- Procurement: please share your standard BAA template or we can propose one — I attached a first-pass BAA-Draft-Medigenics-v1.docx.
- Security: can we schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive this week so Sean (security lead) and Karthik (solution architect) can answer KMS/encryption and network questions?

Proposed timeline:
- This week: share SOC2 scoping checklist + schedule technical deep-dive.
- 1–2 weeks: agree hosting route (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and BAA redlines.

If helpful I can prepare a short audit playbook document that maps what Redwood can provide for each hosting route (logs, retention, access reviews, KMS flows).

Thanks — feel free to reply with availability.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: SOC2-Report-2024.pdf (stub); BAA-Draft-Medigenics-v1.docx
From: Dr. Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@medigenics.com>

Cc: Medigenics Sec Ops <security@medigenics.com>, Procurement <procurement@medigenics.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Medigenics — hosting route & audit playbook

Neha — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side before the tech call: 

1) SOC 2: our auditors will want control mappings for Logical & Physical Access, Encryption (KMS), Change Management, and Logging/Monitoring. Can you confirm which controls in your SOC 2 map to these categories? A control-ID-to-description mapping would be ideal.

2) BAA: Procurement prefers we start from our template but will accept redlines. I attached our internal checklist separately to the Sec Ops mailbox.

3) Private hosting: our security lead is concerned about key ownership. If we move to Private VPC, we need customer-managed KMS with no Redwood access to master keys. Is that supported?

We are available for a technical call Wed 5/5 9:00–11:00 PT.

—Laura
Dr. Laura Simmons
Head of Product Security | Medigenics
laura.simmons@medigenics.com
+1 (617) 555-4401
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dr. Laura Simmons <laura.simmons@medigenics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Medigenics Sec Ops <security@medigenics.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Medigenics — hosting route & audit playbook

Laura — perfect, thanks. Short answers up front: 
- SOC 2 mapping: yes — we can produce a control mapping doc that aligns our SOC 2 sections to the categories you listed (Logical Access, KMS, Change Mgmt, Logging). I'll have Karthik and Sean bring specifics to Wed's call.
- Customer KMS: supported on Private VPC deployments — we offer a configuration where you supply a customer-managed KMS (cloud KMS or HSM) and our services encrypt using a wrapped key. For Dedicated capacity we can also offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) options but with limited operator-level access controls.

Prep for Wed 5/5 call (30 min):
- Agenda: 1) SOC2 control mapping (10 min) 2) KMS/key ownership and network flow (10 min) 3) Timeline & procurement milestones (10 min)
- Attendees: Neha, Marissa (CS lead), Karthik (Solutions), Sean (Security) + Laura + one Sec Ops rep + one Procurement contact

I've created a shared Drive folder for evidence exchange and placed the BAA draft there: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cMedigenics-evidence

Will send calendar invite once you confirm Wed slot.

Regards,
Neha
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 07:34:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Medigenics — hosting route & audit playbook (internal)

Internal note prior to Wed call — key points to surface: 

1) SOC 2 evidence: prepare the following artifacts in advance so we can accelerate procurement:
   - SOC2 Type II report (PDF) + controls matrix (CSV)
   - Encryption key management diagram (who holds CMK, rotation policy)
   - Logging & retention table (what events we capture, retention windows per tier)

2) Private VPC KMS flow: bring-your-own-key supported via customer-managed KMS (Cloud KMS or AWS KMS external key). We must document that Redwood has no access to the unwrapped key material; we only receive wrapped keys or a key-encrypting key (KEK).

3) Dedicated capacity: highlight that Dedicated provides tenant isolation and SLA uplift but still requires Redwood-managed infrastructure — note the difference vs Private where we hand over network & KMS boundaries.

Action items for us before the call:
- Karthik: draft a 1-page KMS flow diagram (attachment: deployment-network-diagram.png stub).
- Marissa: prepare a short note on typical SLA uplift and estimated lead time for Dedicated provisioning (3–4 weeks).
- Neha: have the BAA draft and the Drive link ready for procurement.

Thanks — will join the Wed 9:00 PT slot.

Sean
Security Lead | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com

- Deliverables on call: SOC2 control mapping (PDF), KMS flow diagram (PNG stub), Dedicated provisioning lead-time (slide).
- Evidence handoff process: once you confirm the scope we'll copy relevant artifacts to the shared Drive folder and create a read-only evidence bundle for your auditors.
- Procurement: we will accept your BAA template; Neha has uploaded our redline in the Drive folder. Procurement can loop DocuSign after a final redline pass.

Next steps after the call: 1) Redwood to populate control mapping doc and provide any missing items; 2) Procurement to exchange BAA redlines; 3) If you choose Private hosting, we will start network onboarding and KMS key exchange flow (timeline 4–6 weeks).
